annotations.note: FY25 rev ~$4.0-4.3bn, EBITDA ~$1.2-1.3bn, backlog $20bn, S&P adj leverage <1.5x -> upgraded to BB+.
Issued $600m 3.5Y 6.125% sukuk via Alpha Star Holding X in Jan 2026 and redeemed $400m early-2026 sukuk; rated Ba1 Stable (Moody's) / BB+ (S&P).

Cash balances include project escrow accounts protected under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007. Disbursements require independent engineer certification against construction progress, insulating project assets from corporate creditors.
Off-plan revenue recognized strictly under IFRS 15 percentage-of-completion. Massive contracted backlog provides 2.5-3.5 years of forward revenue coverage.
Land bank held at historical acquisition cost; revalued market appraisal provides substantial asset cushion (>3.0x net debt).

verdict.summary: S&P upgraded DAMAC to BB+ backed by ~$20bn revenue backlog, ~$4.0-4.3bn FY25 revenue, ~$1.2-1.3bn EBITDA, and S&P-adjusted debt/EBITDA below 1.5x. Cycle sensitivity to Dubai luxury presales and private-owner dividend/land outflows remain key watchpoints.

positives: Rated Ba1 Stable (Moody's) / BB+ (S&P) — one notch below investment grade, supported by ultra-low net leverage (~0.3x).
Jan 2026 $600m 6.125% 3.5Y sukuk priced cleanly inside prior coupon tiers and cleared early-2026 $400m maturity.
Multi-year Dubai residential sales backlog and escrow cash collections provide high revenue visibility.
negatives: Heavy geographic concentration in cyclical Dubai luxury/branded residential real estate.
Large off-plan construction commitments & land bank replenishment capex can absorb cash if pre-sales cool.
Private controlling ownership (Hussain Sajwani) poses discretionary dividend/data-center capex risk.
